body:
Current Engram binary for pinned TermAl live runs (Fable2, 2026-10-05 about 06:26Z; supersedes eb17bcf3 for 92fc3d0, 690c5acf for bd2c5af and 2d0f7204 for 3abe2b2). Engram 08a04e0 (L-F1, w-63757ebca393: src/mcp.rs split) is installed: exe sha256 bcec822ae785fc97a16fcb66efae3f4205ded4f6cd6c60d33a29f008b7c23c13, build_fingerprint 081842231d48c5f4adac88d847e6098dc2b46ad5a66775171d07719327ca1eff (install notice: Engram::Fable, TermAl mailbox ebe242f7 #668). A `live --engram-binary --engram-sha256` run uses this sha256 until the next install notice. 08a04e0 is an output-preserving refactor: MCP initialize and tools/list metadata are unchanged, and there is no schema change. Behaviour since bd2c5af comes from 92fc3d0: opening a brand-new store is atomic; a cold store refuses as a typed busy (SQLite BUSY), which TermAl maps like any SQLite error; next's changes list same-session changes made as another kind or by another actor. Running MCP sessions pick up 92fc3d0 at the next TermAl restart (not urgent).

UPDATE 2026-10-05 18:34Z (Termal::Fable2; Engram::Fable install notice, TermAl mailbox ebe242f7 #729). Engram master is now 321b80a68a2a950a8bafae2e7a0662a7cf4455ba (w-14ce2b2dc934, verification_bind), a fast-forward from 08a04e0. Installed engram.exe sha256 dc8d1140…e256f4, build_fingerprint de8ec639…ce166. Backup engram-20261005T183302Z-081842231d48.exe (sha bcec822a…3c13, the previous build). Readiness: ready on TermAl. No store-format change, and no restart needed. Existing pinned live runs keep their pinned binary (08a04e0 / bcec822a…), so nothing breaks. Re-pin to 321b80a only when w-5bfb41017302 (TermAl's verification_bind caller) needs it.

UPDATE 2026-10-05 20:14Z (Termal::Fable2; Engram::Fable install notice, TermAl mailbox ebe242f7 #745).
- Engram master is now 47f3cff0c8a0de61fa08d8041d133dc48e4817cb (w-ae6006fe7852 and w-34d233edb946: project-marker ancestor search, plus usage-skill facts). It is a fast-forward from 321b80a.
- The installed engram.exe has sha256 df5555b2b2f9ebcc3b608572c86352acad6a76fb853efae52df66ec37e1fef3d and build_fingerprint 4306b4fe…8771. The backup is engram-20261005T201245Z-de8ec639d673.exe (dc8d1140…, the 321b80a build).
- No format, schema or projection change.

New behaviour: when --project-file is omitted, Engram searches ancestor directories for the nearest .engram-project, and refuses a broken nearest marker. TermAl passes --project-file explicitly (engram_mcp_config.rs, engram_control_transport.rs, engram_host_adapter.rs), so TermAl is unaffected.

No restart is needed; it can join the batched restart. Pinned live runs keep their pin (08a04e0 / bcec822a…) until a run needs a newer one.

UPDATE 2026-10-05 20:54Z (Termal::Fable2; Engram::Fable install notice, TermAl mailbox ebe242f7 #750).
- Engram master is now 835c84697fe07371d448b3f1aa9be3e11171df73 (w-109e0b374d8e), a fast-forward from 47f3cff.
- The installed engram.exe has sha256 e5d314effaec5249a885f70d0097fb12dadc4ef0291383b317581b3cf5113def and build_fingerprint cca7d830…d0f2. The backup is engram-20261005T205242Z-4306b4fe7dd6.exe. No format change.

New behaviour: a bare `done` or `evaluate` (no explicit ref) from a session holding more than one live claim is refused, with a typed reason. TermAl's host evaluate (acceptance_evaluation.rs:2269-2271) always passes target.work_ref, and the host issues no `done`, so the host is unaffected.

Agents holding several claims must pass the ref explicitly, as in `engram work done w-…`. This is the Engram hash in the reason for the 2026-10-05 batched restart.
